pairs.name: Two members of M2026-A1
pairs.blurb: The tightest pair among the first 120 GMN members of the new stream.
pairs.verdict: Tiny on every criterion — and this pair is part of a real stream. But that verdict did not come from these numbers. It came from the population: 282 members sitting in a pair excess measured against a 122,943-meteor null and surviving a 400-cell correction at 5.3σ (ApJ 1000, 254).

pairs.name: Příbram – Neuschwanstein
pairs.blurb: The famous claimed meteorite pair: fell 43 years apart on near-identical orbits. Every criterion calls it a match.
pairs.verdict: Just as tiny on every criterion — and not significant. Among a few hundred fireball orbits a D′ this small (≈ 0.009) turns up by chance about 70% of the time (Pauls & Gladman 2005), and the pair fails a 3σ test against a KDE null (A&A 693, A23). Same numbers as the stream pair; opposite verdict. The difference is the population, not the orbits.

pairs.name: A stream member vs. a sporadic
pairs.blurb: What an unrelated pair looks like, for scale.
pairs.verdict: Large on every criterion. Nobody would call this a pair — but notice that this is the only kind of case the four numbers can settle on their own. They cannot tell the first two presets apart.
